memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"It must be eaten inside the house; take none of the meat outside the house. Do
not break any of the bones." - Ex 12:46 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two small instructions, and one of them becomes one of the most striking
prophecies in the Bible.

"Do not break any of the bones." Why would God specify this? In practical terms,
it kept the lamb whole and undivided. But John, standing at the cross, saw
something more.

Roman soldiers routinely broke the legs of crucified men to hasten death. They
did this to the two thieves. But when they came to Jesus, He had already died,
so they did not break His legs. John writes: "These things happened so that the
scripture would be fulfilled: 'Not one of his bones will be broken'" (John
19:36).

Consider that. Roman soldiers, with no knowledge of Exodus and no interest in
Jewish scripture, made a battlefield decision that fulfilled a regulation given
fifteen hundred years earlier about a lamb.

That is the kind of God we serve. He wrote the details of His Son's death into a
dinner instruction given to slaves in Egypt, and then brought it to pass through
the hands of men who had never read it.

Nothing about the cross was improvised.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does the precision of prophecy strengthen your confidence in Scripture?
2. What in your life feels random that God may be weaving into a larger plan?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You wrote the story before it happened. Thank You that the cross was no
accident. Strengthen my trust in Your Word. Amen.
